task: Fix the one red acceptance case of DAEO-u4oz (W2-04), success-7 `test_further_batch_is_at_most_one_batch_long`, against S7/S7a
status: DONE — the case's expectation is within S7/S7a; the build is fixed, the unit tests are green and `gov accept` passes on all seven KPI lines
work_completed: I judged the case within the specification. S7 defines `further_batch` as "the ranked items that were not stacked for lack of room, beginning with the first one that did not fit, at most one batch long". S7a says "the batches' items taken together, in order, are the rank order" and that `further_batch` starts at the first ranked item that was not stacked. A list that names items no batch read (`ranked[left_from:left_from + width]` with width 10) goes past that sequence. I changed `stack()` in `src/gov/retrieval/supplementary.py` so that `further_batch = ranked[left_from:taken]`: the last batch's items from the first one that did not fit. That makes it at most one batch long by construction (it is never longer than that batch's `limit`, so never longer than the largest `limit`). It holds no stacked item and keeps strict rank order. It is deterministic. I removed the branch that named unread items when the room hit 0 (`room == 0 and taken < len(ranked)`) and updated the module docstring. Edge case I chose: when no batch can be taken (room 0 after the mandatory inputs), or the room runs out exactly on a full batch's last item, then `supplementary_batches` holds only the batches taken (empty for room 0) and `further_batch == []`. `dropped` gets no budget entry either. No item failed to fit, and an unread item is never named. This follows S7's "beginning with the first one that did not fit" (there is none) and S7a's bound by the largest `limit` (with no batch there is no limit). The cost is that evidence which remains past an exact fit is not named. When the room runs out partway through a batch, the item after the last stacked one does not fit, so it and the rest of that batch are named as before.

One existing test that expected the old behaviour was rewritten to the specified behaviour, and three tests were added: further_batch names only items a batch read (a smaller second batch); room that ends on a batch's last item names nothing; no room takes no batch and names nothing. Acceptance, `gov accept DAEO-u4oz --json` (exit 0, outcome pass): success-1 pass 8/0/0; success-2 pass 7/0/1 skipped; success-3 pass 5/0/0; success-4 pass 7/0/1 skipped; success-5 pass 11/0/0; success-6 pass 2/0/0; success-7 pass 10/0/0; unmapped 9 passed; totals 59 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (passed/failed/skipped).
discoveries: When room was left in tokens, the old code also named up to 10 items beyond what any batch read whenever the stack stopped partway through a batch whose `limit` was below the largest `limit`. That is the failing case.
risks: In the exact-fit and room-0 cases `further_batch` is now empty although ranked evidence may remain. This is my reading of S7/S7a; it is reversible by one line if the lead or CTO wants a different choice. The lexical lookup still runs when the room is 0, so a lookup failure is still named in `dropped`, as before.
lessons: In `stack()` a "batch" is a slice of the full ranked list; only what appears in `supplementary_batches` counts as read for S7a.
proposed_decisions: One choice I made, with no package needed unless the lead disagrees: at room 0, or when the room runs out exactly at the end of a full batch, `further_batch` is `[]` and no batch is taken. Alternative: take a 1-item batch at room 0 so the first unfitting item is named. That conflicts with "no batch is larger than the room can use". Recommendation: keep the current choice; confidence medium-high.
